sanskrit: śivā cāśivasaṃkāśā tasya vaktrāt sudāruṇā niṣpapāta mahāghorā smṛtiḥ sā tasya bhārata ulkāś ca jvalitās tasya dīptāḥ pārśve prapedire
english: A she-jackal, inauspicious of aspect and most dreadful, leapt forth from his mouth—the loss of his very wits, O Bhārata, fearful and terrible. And blazing meteors, flaming bright, fell at his side.

sanskrit: gṛdhrakaṅkavaḍāś caiva vāco 'muñcan sudāruṇāḥ vṛtrasyopari saṃhṛṣṭāś cakravat paribabhramuḥ
english: Vultures, herons, and crows let loose their most dreadful cries, and, exulting, wheeled round and round above Vṛtra like a turning wheel.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ ratham āsthāya devāpyāyitam āhave vajrodyatakaraḥ śakras taṃ daityaṃ pratyavaikṣata
english: Then Śakra, mounting in the battle that chariot empowered by the gods, his thunderbolt raised in his hand, fixed his gaze upon that Daitya.

sanskrit: amānuṣam atho nādaṃ sa mumoca mahāsuraḥ vyajṛmbhata ca rājendra tīvrajvarasamanvitaḥ athāsya jṛmbhataḥ śakras tato vajram avāsṛjat
english: Then that great Asura uttered an unearthly roar and gaped wide, O lord of kings, seized by the fierce fever; and as he gaped, Śakra hurled the thunderbolt upon him.

sanskrit: sa vajraḥ sumahātejāḥ kālāgnisadṛśopamaḥ kṣipram eva mahākāyaṃ vṛtraṃ daityam apātayat
english: That thunderbolt of mighty splendour, like unto the fire of universal doom, swiftly struck down the vast-bodied Daitya Vṛtra.

sanskrit: tato nādaḥ samabhavat punar eva samantataḥ vṛtraṃ vinihataṃ dṛṣṭvā devānāṃ bharatarṣabha
english: Then once more a great cry arose on every side from the gods, O bull of the Bharatas, when they beheld Vṛtra slain.

sanskrit: vṛtraṃ tu hatvā bhagavān dānavārir mahāyaśāḥ vajreṇa viṣṇuyuktena divam eva samāviśat
english: Having slain Vṛtra with the thunderbolt charged with Viṣṇu's power, the illustrious lord, foe of the Dānavas, ascended into heaven itself.

sanskrit: atha vṛtrasya kauravya śarīrād abhiniḥsṛtā brahmahatyā mahāghorā raudrā lokabhayāvahā
english: Then from Vṛtra's body, O Kaurava, there issued forth Brahmahatyā—the sin of brahmin-slaughter—most terrible, savage, a terror to the worlds.

sanskrit: karāladaśanā bhīmā vikṛtā kṛṣṇapiṅgalā prakīrṇamūrdhajā caiva ghoranetrā ca bhārata
english: With jagged teeth, dreadful, deformed, black and tawny, her hair flying loose, her eyes terrible, O Bhārata,

sanskrit: kapālamālinī caiva kṛśā ca bharatarṣabha rudhirārdrā ca dharmajña cīravastranivāsinī
english: garlanded with skulls and gaunt, O bull of the Bharatas, drenched in blood, O knower of dharma, clad in rags she was.

sanskrit: sābhiniṣkramya rājendra tādṛgrūpā bhayāvahā vajriṇaṃ mṛgayām āsa tadā bharatasattama
english: Coming forth in that fearful shape, O lord of kings, she then set out in search of the wielder of the thunderbolt, O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: kasya cit tv atha kālasya vṛtrahā kurunandana svargāyābhimukhaḥ prāyāl lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā
english: After a certain time, O delight of the Kurus, the slayer of Vṛtra set forth toward heaven, desiring the welfare of the worlds.

sanskrit: bisān niḥsaramāṇaṃ tu dṛṣṭvā śakraṃ mahaujasam kaṇṭhe jagrāha devendraṃ sulagnā cābhavat tadā
english: But seeing the mighty Śakra slipping away among the lotus-stalks, she seized the king of the gods by the throat and clung fast to him.

sanskrit: sa hi tasmin samutpanne brahmahatyākṛte bhaye nalinyāṃ bisamadhyastho babhūvābdagaṇān bahūn
english: For when that terror wrought by the slaying of a brahmin had arisen, he dwelt within a lotus-pond, hidden in the midst of the stalks, for many years.

sanskrit: anusṛtya tu yatnāt sa tayā vai brahmahatyayā tadā gṛhītaḥ kauravya niśceṣṭaḥ samapadyata
english: But that Brahmahatyā, having tracked him down with effort, seized him then, O Kaurava, and he became motionless and helpless.

sanskrit: tasyā vyapohane śakraḥ paraṃ yatnaṃ cakāra ha na cāśakat tāṃ devendro brahmahatyāṃ vyapohitum
english: Śakra made the utmost effort to be rid of her, yet the king of the gods could not drive off that Brahmahatyā.

sanskrit: gṛhīta eva tu tayā devendro bharatarṣabha pitāmaham upāgamya śirasā pratyapūjayat
english: Held fast by her, O bull of the Bharatas, the king of the gods approached the Grandsire and did him homage, bowing his head.

sanskrit: jñātvā gṛhītaṃ śakraṃ tu dvijapravarahatyayā brahmā saṃcintayām āsa tadā bharatasattama
english: Knowing that Śakra was held fast by the sin of slaying a foremost of the twice-born, Brahmā then fell to pondering, O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tām uvāca mahābāho brahmahatyāṃ pitāmahaḥ svareṇa madhureṇātha sāntvayann iva bhārata
english: O mighty-armed one, the Grandsire then addressed that Brahmahatyā in a sweet voice, as if to soothe her, O Bhārata:

sanskrit: mucyatāṃ tridaśendro 'yaṃ matpriyaṃ kuru bhāmini brūhi kiṃ te karomy adya kāmaṃ kaṃ tvam ihecchasi
english: "Let this lord of the thirty gods be released; do me this kindness, O passionate one. Tell me, what shall I do for you this day? What desire of yours would you have fulfilled herein?"

sanskrit: brahmahatyovāca trilokapūjite deve prīte trailokyakartari kṛtam eveha manye 'haṃ nivāsaṃ tu vidhatsva me
english: Brahmahatyā said: "Since the god worshipped in the three worlds, the maker of the threefold world, is pleased, I deem my purpose here already accomplished—only ordain me a dwelling-place."

sanskrit: tvayā kṛteyaṃ maryādā lokasaṃrakṣaṇārthinā sthāpanā vai sumahatī tvayā deva pravartitā
english: "This boundary has been set by you, who seek the protection of the worlds; a most weighty ordinance has been established and set in motion by you, O god."

sanskrit: prīte tu tvayi dharmajña sarvalokeśvare prabho śakrād apagamiṣyāmi nivāsaṃ tu vidhatsva me
english: "Since you are pleased, O knower of dharma, lord of all the worlds, O master, I shall depart from Śakra—only ordain me a dwelling-place."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tatheti tāṃ prāha tadā brahmahatyāṃ pitāmahaḥ upāyataḥ sa śakrasya brahmahatyāṃ vyapohata
english: Bhīṣma said: "So be it," the Grandsire then said to that Brahmahatyā, and by a skilful expedient he drove the brahmin-slaughter away from Śakra.

sanskrit: tataḥ svayaṃbhuvā dhyātas tatra vahnir mahātmanā brahmāṇam upasaṃgamya tato vacanam abravīt
english: Then Fire, summoned in thought by the high-souled Self-Existent One, drew near to Brahmā and spoke these words:

sanskrit: prāpto 'smi bhagavan deva tvatsakāśam ariṃdama yat kartavyaṃ mayā deva tad bhavān vaktum arhati
english: "I have come into your presence, O blessed god, O subduer of foes. What is to be done by me, O god, that you should be pleased to declare."

sanskrit: brahmovāca bahudhā vibhajiṣyāmi brahmahatyām imām aham śakrasyādya vimokṣārthaṃ caturbhāgaṃ pratīccha me
english: Brahmā said: "I shall divide this Brahmahatyā into many parts. For the release of Śakra this day, accept from me a fourth portion of her."

sanskrit: agnir uvāca mama mokṣasya ko 'nto vai brahman dhyāyasva vai prabho etad icchāmi vijñātuṃ tattvato lokapūjita
english: Agni said: "What is to be the end of my release, O Brahman? Reflect upon it, O master. This I wish to know truly, O you who are worshipped by the worlds."

sanskrit: brahmovāca yas tvāṃ jvalantam āsādya svayaṃ vai mānavaḥ kva cit bījauṣadhirasair vahne na yakṣyati tamovṛtaḥ
english: Brahmā said: "Whatever man, drawing near to you when you blaze, shall fail of his own accord to make offering anywhere with the saps of seeds and herbs, O Fire, being veiled in darkness of mind—

sanskrit: tam eṣā yāsyati kṣipraṃ tatraiva ca nivatsyati brahmahatyā havyavāha vyetu te mānaso jvaraḥ
english: to him she shall swiftly pass, O bearer of oblations, and there shall she abide. Let the fever of your mind depart."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ity uktaḥ pratijagrāha tad vaco havyakavyabhuk pitāmahasya bhagavāṃs tathā ca tad abhūt prabho
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus addressed, the blessed bearer of offerings to gods and ancestors accepted the word of the Grandsire, and so it came to pass, O lord.

sanskrit: tato vṛkṣauṣadhitṛṇaṃ samāhūya pitāmahaḥ imam arthaṃ mahārāja vaktuṃ samupacakrame
english: Then the Grandsire, summoning trees, herbs, and grasses, began to declare this matter to them, O great king.

sanskrit: tato vṛkṣauṣadhitṛṇaṃ tathaivoktaṃ yathātatham vyathitaṃ vahnivad rājan brahmāṇam idam abravīt
english: Then the trees, herbs, and grasses, being told the matter just as it was, were troubled as Fire had been, O king, and spoke thus to Brahmā:

sanskrit: asmākaṃ brahmahatyāto ko 'nto lokapitāmaha svabhāvanihatān asmān na punar hantum arhasi
english: "What is to be the end for us of this Brahmahatyā, O Grandsire of the worlds? Slain already by our own nature, we ought not to be slain by you again."

sanskrit: vayam agniṃ tathā śītaṃ varṣaṃ ca pavaneritam sahāmaḥ satataṃ deva tathā chedanabhedanam
english: "We endure forever fire and cold and rain driven by the wind, O god, and the cutting and splitting too."

sanskrit: brahmahatyām imām adya bhavataḥ śāsanād vayam grahīṣyāmas trilokeśa mokṣaṃ cintayatāṃ bhavān
english: "This Brahmahatyā we shall take upon ourselves this day at your command, O lord of the three worlds; but let your honour consider our release."

sanskrit: brahmovāca parvakāle tu saṃprāpte yo vai chedanabhedanam kariṣyati naro mohāt tam eṣānugamiṣyati
english: Brahmā said: "When the sacred season of the moon's change has come, whatever man shall in his folly perform cutting and splitting, her she shall follow."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tato vṛkṣauṣadhitṛṇam evam uktaṃ mahātmanā brahmāṇam abhisaṃpūjya jagāmāśu yathāgatam
english: Bhīṣma said: Then the trees, herbs, and grasses, thus addressed by the high-souled one, paid homage to Brahmā and swiftly departed as they had come.

sanskrit: āhūyāpsaraso devas tato lokapitāmahaḥ vācā madhurayā prāha sāntvayann iva bhārata
english: Then the god, the Grandsire of the worlds, summoning the Apsarases, spoke to them in a sweet voice, as if to soothe them, O Bhārata:

sanskrit: iyam indrād anuprāptā brahmahatyā varāṅganāḥ caturtham asyā bhāgaṃ hi mayoktāḥ saṃpratīcchata
english: "This Brahmahatyā has passed to me from Indra, O fair-limbed ones. So bidden by me, accept a fourth portion of her."

sanskrit: apsarasa ūcuḥ grahaṇe kṛtabuddhīnāṃ deveśa tava śāsanāt mokṣaṃ samayato 'smākaṃ cintayasva pitāmaha
english: The Apsarases said: "Since we are resolved to take her on at your command, O lord of the gods, consider, O Grandsire, our release upon condition."

sanskrit: brahmovāca rajasvalāsu nārīṣu yo vai maithunam ācaret tam eṣā yāsyati kṣipraṃ vyetu vo mānaso jvaraḥ
english: Brahmā said: "Whatever man shall have intercourse with women in their courses, to him she shall swiftly pass. Let the fever of your minds depart."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tatheti hṛṣṭamanasa uktvāthāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ svāni sthānāni saṃprāpya remire bharatarṣabha
english: Bhīṣma said: Saying "So be it" with gladdened hearts, the troops of Apsarases reached their own abodes and made merry, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tatas trilokakṛd devaḥ punar eva mahātapāḥ apaḥ saṃcintayām āsa dhyātās tāś cāpy athāgaman
english: Then the god of mighty austerity, maker of the three worlds, once more called the Waters to mind, and being so summoned they came.

sanskrit: tās tu sarvāḥ samāgamya brahmāṇam amitaujasam idam ūcur vaco rājan praṇipatya pitāmaham
english: And all of them, gathering before Brahmā of measureless might, bowed down to the Grandsire and spoke this word, O king:

sanskrit: imāḥ sma deva saṃprāptās tvatsakāśam ariṃdama śāsanāt tava deveśa samājñāpaya no vibho
english: "Here are we come into your presence, O god, O subduer of foes, at your command, O lord of the gods. Lay your charge upon us, O all-pervading one."

sanskrit: brahmovāca iyaṃ vṛtrād anuprāptā puruhūtaṃ mahābhayā brahmahatyā caturthāṃśam asyā yūyaṃ pratīcchata
english: Brahmā said: "This Brahmahatyā of great terror has passed from Vṛtra to him of the many invocations. Do you accept a fourth portion of her."

sanskrit: āpa ūcuḥ evaṃ bhavatu lokeśa yathā vadasi naḥ prabho mokṣaṃ samayato 'smākaṃ saṃcintayitum arhasi
english: The Waters said: "So be it, O lord of the worlds, as you bid us, O master; but you ought to consider our release upon condition."

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi deveśa sarvasya jagataḥ paramo guruḥ ko 'nyaḥ prasādo hi bhaved yaḥ kṛcchrān naḥ samuddharet
english: "For you, O lord of the gods, are the supreme preceptor of all the world. What other grace could there be that would deliver us from distress?"

sanskrit: brahmovāca alpā iti matiṃ kṛtvā yo naro buddhimohitaḥ śleṣmamūtrapurīṣāṇi yuṣmāsu pratimokṣyati
english: Brahmā said: "Whatever man, deeming you of slight account in his deluded mind, shall cast phlegm, urine, and excrement into you—

sanskrit: tam eṣā yāsyati kṣipraṃ tatraiva ca nivatsyati tathā vo bhavitā mokṣa iti satyaṃ bravīmi vaḥ
english: to him she shall swiftly pass, and there shall she abide. Thus shall your release come to be—this I tell you in truth."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tato vimucya devendraṃ brahmahatyā yudhiṣṭhira yathānisṛṣṭaṃ taṃ deśam agacchad devaśāsanāt
english: Bhīṣma said: Then Brahmahatyā, releasing the king of the gods, O Yudhiṣṭhira, went to the place assigned her, at the god's command.

sanskrit: evaṃ śakreṇa saṃprāptā brahmahatyā janādhipa pitāmaham anujñāpya so 'śvamedham akalpayat
english: Thus, O ruler of men, did Brahmahatyā come upon Śakra; and having taken leave of the Grandsire, he performed the Horse Sacrifice.

sanskrit: śrūyate hi mahārāja saṃprāptā vāsavena vai brahmahatyā tataḥ śuddhiṃ hayamedhena labdhavān
english: For it is heard, O great king, that Brahmahatyā came upon Vāsava, and thereafter he won purification by the Horse Sacrifice.

sanskrit: samavāpya śriyaṃ devo hatvārīṃś ca sahasraśaḥ praharṣam atulaṃ lebhe vāsavaḥ pṛthivīpate
english: Having regained his royal fortune and slain his foes by thousands, the god Vāsava attained joy beyond compare, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: vṛtrasya rudhirāc caiva khukhuṇḍāḥ pārtha jajñire dvijātibhir abhakṣyās te dīkṣitaiś ca tapodhanaiḥ
english: And from Vṛtra's blood, O Pārtha, were born the mushrooms, which are not to be eaten by the twice-born, by the consecrated, or by those rich in austerity.

sanskrit: sarvāvasthaṃ tvam apy eṣāṃ dvijātīnāṃ priyaṃ kuru ime hi bhūtale devāḥ prathitāḥ kurunandana
english: You too in every circumstance should do what is dear to these twice-born; for they are gods made manifest upon the earth, O delight of the Kurus.

sanskrit: evaṃ śakreṇa kauravya buddhisaukṣmyān mahāsuraḥ upāyapūrvaṃ nihato vṛtro 'thāmitatejasā
english: Thus, O Kaurava, by Śakra of measureless splendour, through subtlety of intellect and by skilful means, was the great Asura Vṛtra slain.

sanskrit: evaṃ tvam api kauravya pṛthivyām aparājitaḥ bhaviṣyasi yathā devaḥ śatakratur amitrahā
english: Even so, O Kaurava, shall you too be unconquered upon the earth, like the god of the hundred sacrifices, the slayer of foes.

sanskrit: ye tu śakrakathāṃ divyām imāṃ parvasu parvasu vipramadhye paṭhiṣyanti na te prāpsyanti kilbiṣam
english: And those who shall recite this divine tale of Śakra, season after season, in the midst of the brahmins, shall incur no sin.

sanskrit: ity etad vṛtram āśritya śakrasyātyadbhutaṃ mahat kathitaṃ karma te tāta kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotum icchasi
english: Thus, with Vṛtra for its theme, this most wondrous and mighty deed of Śakra has been told to you, my son. What more do you wish to hear?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca pitāmaha mahāprājña sarvaśāstraviśārada asti vṛtravadhād eva vivakṣā mama jāyate
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: O Grandsire, greatly wise, versed in all the sciences, from the very slaying of Vṛtra a question arises that I would put to you.

sanskrit: jvareṇa mohito vṛtraḥ kathitas te janādhipa nihato vāsaveneha vajreṇeti mamānagha
english: Vṛtra, bewildered by fever, was described by you, O ruler of men, as slain here by Vāsava with the thunderbolt, O sinless one.

sanskrit: katham eṣa mahāprājña jvaraḥ prādurabhūt kutaḥ jvarotpattiṃ nipuṇataḥ śrotum icchāmy ahaṃ prabho
english: How, O greatly wise one, did this fever come to be, and whence? I wish to hear with precision the origin of fever, O master.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca śṛṇu rājañ jvarasyeha saṃbhavaṃ lokaviśrutam vistaraṃ cāsya vakṣyāmi yādṛśaṃ caiva bhārata
english: Bhīṣma said: Hear, O king, the origin of fever, renowned throughout the world; and I shall tell its full account and of what nature it is, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: purā meror mahārāja śṛṅgaṃ trailokyaviśrutam jyotiṣkaṃ nāma sāvitraṃ sarvaratnavibhūṣitam aprameyam anādhṛṣyaṃ sarvalokeṣu bhārata
english: Of old, O great king, there was a peak of Meru, famed throughout the three worlds, named Jyotiṣka, belonging to the Sun, adorned with every gem, immeasurable and unassailable in all the worlds, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tatra devo giritaṭe hemadhātuvibhūṣite paryaṅka iva vibhrājann upaviṣṭo babhūva ha
english: There upon the mountain-slope, adorned with veins of gold, the god sat, shining as though upon a couch.

sanskrit: śailarājasutā cāsya nityaṃ pārśve sthitā babhau tathā devā mahātmāno vasavaś ca mahaujasaḥ
english: And the daughter of the mountain-king, ever stationed at his side, shone there; and so too the high-souled gods and the mighty Vasus.

sanskrit: tathaiva ca mahātmānāv aśvinau bhiṣajāṃ varau tathā vaiśravaṇo rājā guhyakair abhisaṃvṛtaḥ
english: And likewise the high-souled Aśvins, best of physicians, and King Vaiśravaṇa, surrounded by the Guhyakas,

sanskrit: yakṣāṇām adhipaḥ śrīmān kailāsanilayaḥ prabhuḥ aṅgiraḥpramukhāś caiva tathā devarṣayo 'pare
english: the glorious lord of the Yakṣas, whose abode is Kailāsa, the master; and the divine sages headed by Aṅgiras, and others besides,

sanskrit: viśvāvasuś ca gandharvas tathā nāradaparvatau apsarogaṇasaṃghāś ca samājagmur anekaśaḥ
english: and the Gandharva Viśvāvasu, and Nārada and Parvata, and hosts upon hosts of Apsarases came together in great numbers.

sanskrit: vavau śivaḥ sukho vāyur nānāgandhavahaḥ śuciḥ sarvartukusumopetāḥ puṣpavanto mahādrumāḥ
english: A gentle, pleasant wind blew, pure and bearing manifold fragrances; and the great trees, in flower, were laden with the blossoms of every season.

sanskrit: tathā vidyādharāś caiva siddhāś caiva tapodhanāḥ mahādevaṃ paśupatiṃ paryupāsanta bhārata
english: And likewise the Vidyādharas, and the Siddhas rich in austerity, waited reverently upon the great god, the Lord of Creatures, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: bhūtāni ca mahārāja nānārūpadharāṇy atha rākṣasāś ca mahāraudrāḥ piśācāś ca mahābalāḥ
english: And the spirits, O great king, wearing manifold shapes, and the most savage Rākṣasas, and the mighty Piśācas,

sanskrit: bahurūpadharā hṛṣṭā nānāpraharaṇodyatāḥ devasyānucarās tatra tasthire cānalopamāḥ
english: the god's attendants, wearing many forms, joyful, raising weapons of every kind, stood there like blazing fire.

sanskrit: nandī ca bhagavāṃs tatra devasyānumate sthitaḥ pragṛhya jvalitaṃ śūlaṃ dīpyamānaṃ svatejasā
english: And the blessed Nandī stood there too, by the god's leave, grasping a blazing trident shining with its own splendour.

sanskrit: gaṅgā ca saritāṃ śreṣṭhā sarvatīrthajalodbhavā paryupāsata taṃ devaṃ rūpiṇī kurunandana
english: And Gaṅgā, best of rivers, arising from the waters of all holy fords, in embodied form waited reverently upon that god, O delight of the Kurus.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa bhagavāṃs tatra pūjyamānaḥ surarṣibhiḥ devaiś ca sumahābhāgair mahādevo vyatiṣṭhata
english: Thus that blessed Mahādeva abode there, worshipped by the divine sages and by the most exalted gods.

sanskrit: kasya cit tv atha kālasya dakṣo nāma prajāpatiḥ pūrvoktena vidhānena yakṣyamāṇo 'nvapadyata
english: Then after a certain time the Prajāpati named Dakṣa set about to perform a sacrifice according to the ordinance aforesaid.

sanskrit: tatas tasya makhaṃ devāḥ sarve śakrapurogamāḥ gamanāya samāgamya buddhim āpedire tadā
english: Then all the gods, with Śakra at their head, gathering together, set their minds upon going to his sacrifice.
